name: The Commodore's Smashed Pocket-Watch
description: A gold open-face pocket-watch lying in the port corner of the stateroom, smashed, stopped at 22:41, and stickier than a toffee apple. A brown smear trails behind it. The crown is pulled out, the way you would set a watch, not the way a fall would leave it.
discoveryLine: Whoever broke this watch was very, very specific about the time.

name: Speech Notes for The Announcement
description: The Commodore's speech notes, written in orange crayon and enthusiasm, each item with a marmalade thumbprint. 1. Percy OUT of the will. Crew pension fund IN. (Tell her gently: ha!) 2. Decline Pratt's £200,000. Launch Brine's Pickled Onions. SQUASH HER. 3. Scrap the Tallyho at Port Pottle. Pay off the crew. 4. The Turnip Scandal. Sack Boris. Say I knew nothing. 5. CROCK 13. False bottom!! Gold!!! Somebody is smuggling in MY marmalade. Tiny mark stamped underneath. Expose at midnight. In the margin: 21:45 Z. (the fee. And the OTHER thing. Face him.) / 22:30 Pratt (let her wait) / 23:30 Capt. B. (the crates. Ask him straight.) / 24:00 SPEAK.
discoveryLine: Five items, five marmalade thumbprints, and a schedule in the margin.
lockedLine: The desk has a speech-shaped hole. The Commodore hid his notes where only someone close to him would know to look. Ask someone who knew his habits.

name: The Marmalade Run
description: Marmalade has a story to tell. The pool by the starboard wall is where the tasting jar burst; it ran downhill and set there, so the room was leaning starboard when it broke. A long brown skid runs from the starboard wall across the carpet towards port, and stops dead against the Commodore: the sea chest is parked on his coat-tail. A chest that slid when the ship swung over would have gone all the way to the port wall, unless somebody was already lying in its way.
discoveryLine: The pool points one way, the skid the other, and the chest is sitting on a dead man's coat-tail.
lockedLine: Marmalade everywhere, and it plainly has something to say. You need to know which way downhill pointed, and when that changed.

name: The Heel Recorder Chart
description: A long paper strip with a wobbly pen line. At 21:40 the pen leans one way. At 22:14 it swings across to the other, and a pencilled note says LURCH 22:14. In the margin the engineer has also pencilled 'LEFT POST 21:45 BACK 22:00' and 'LEFT POST 22:30 BACK 22:45'.
discoveryLine: The sea keeps a diary, and somebody has been writing naughty notes in its margin.
lockedLine: The chart is under glass and under a very deadpan glare. "Come back when you know what you're asking. And when we've talked properly."

name: The Cheer-Box
description: A brass box holding an old wind-up phonograph and a wax cylinder labelled 'EMERGENCY CHEER (the one with the hiccup), recorded 1911'. The spring is nearly run down, as if it was wound for a single play. There is no clockwork timer: somebody has to stand here and start it by hand. The junction switch is on CHEER, and the seasick bucket beside it is bone dry. A brass plate on the chartroom door reads: KEYS: MASTER; CHIEF ENGINEER.
discoveryLine: Somebody played the Commodore's voice from this box, tonight, and tidied up badly.
lockedLine: Behind the velvet curtain, a locked door with a brass key plate. You need a reason to ask for that door to be opened.

name: The Course Sheet
description: A chart with a dashed red line. The real course is not Port Pottle: it turns hard at 22:14 and runs to Cape Kipper, and stops. Next to the dawn rendezvous: 'Lugger. Hand over 13 crocks. Collect from the wings.'
discoveryLine: Nothing about this course is straight.
lockedLine: A chart table full of charts. None of them looks strange. You need a reason to hunt for a particular one.

name: Crock 13
description: Behind the prop trunk's false wall: padded trays of gold sovereigns and a rack of thirteen chalk-numbered cradles. Cradle 13 holds a stoneware crock with an orange toupee glued to it like a hat. Its false bottom is full of gold and stamped underneath with a tiny maker's mark: A.Z. The crock has a dent shaped like Barnabas.
discoveryLine: A crock wearing a toupee. Never underestimate a hat.
lockedLine: Seventeen padlocks and a rabbit. Searching without cause would earn you a lawsuit and a bite.

name: The Receipt for Nine Parts Turnip
description: A recipe card in a weepy, tear-smudged hand: 'BRINE'S BITTER ORANGE (SECRET). 1 part orange. 9 parts turnip. Weep.' It is the cook's own working copy. Stapled to it, a note of sale the buyer had to sign before the original changed hands: 'Received, one recipe, for £500 paid. Boat deck, by the rail, 21:50. G. P.-P.'
discoveryLine: The secret of Brine's Bitter Orange is a root vegetable.
lockedLine: The recipe drawers are guarded by a weeping giant: "Not until you understand my pain."

name: The Evidence of Duchess
description: Lifeboat 3 contains a heap of hay dusted with galley flour, a bucket, a trail of cloven hoofprints and a goat who is chewing a pink feather plume you have definitely seen on a young woman's hat.
discoveryLine: The goat looks guilty. The goat looks very pleased with herself.

name: Orange Lightning
description: Behind the boiler, in the pump house, a copper still gurgles merrily. On the shelf stands a heavy round stoneware jug: 'ORANGE LIGHTNING (Strictly Medicinal)'. It smells of marmalade and regret, and the label says it is made from the Commodore's surplus.
discoveryLine: Strictly medicinal, says the label. The smell disagrees.
lockedLine: A bolted hatch behind the boiler, and a smell like a burnt breakfast. You will need a second look.

name: The Deck Log
description: The Tallyho's deck log, in a square, captainly hand. '20:53. Master took the wheel. Helmsman stood down until the middle watch.' '21:40. Squall. Wireless lost. Heeling to starboard.' At 22:14 the course column has been scraped with a razor and inked over, fresher and blacker: 'Heavy sea on the port quarter. Hard-a-port. Course for Port Pottle.' Across the foot of the page, in the same fresh ink: 'Master at the wheel throughout the watch.' Every change of hand at the wheel is logged tonight, but one.
discoveryLine: A man who never left his wheel had no need to write so.
lockedLine: The deck log lies under a brass weight: a whole night of entries in a square hand. You would need to know which minute to look for.
